input: This case presents a review of the transport cost of a regional delivery route, based on the carrier invoices received over the last 12 months. The review has been undertaken in order to establish what the route currently costs the business over a full year of operation, and the figures which follow are drawn entirely from the invoiced record for the period in question. Each trip on the route covers a distance of 862 km, and the invoiced cost of the transport amounts to $1.5 per km, which corresponds to a cost of $1293 for each trip that is undertaken. In total, the route is operated 832 times per year. When these figures are brought together, the annual transport cost of the route is found to be $1076k. It is important to note that the trip count on which this figure is based includes empty running, so that the annual cost represents the cost of all of the running performed on the route, both loaded and empty, taken together, and no part of it can be read as the cost of the loaded running alone. The figure is, in other words, an invoice total for the route exactly as it is currently operated, at the distance, the rate, and the number of trips stated above, and it should be understood on that basis when it is compared with the cost of any alternative arrangement, since an alternative costed on a different basis, for example with empty running treated separately, would not be directly comparable with it.
target: Annual transport cost for the regional delivery route is $1076k, on carrier invoices for the last 12 months. The route runs 832 trips per year. Each trip covers 862 km at an invoiced cost of $1.5 per km, a trip cost of $1293, and the annual figure is the trip cost carried over the year's trips at the stated rate and distance. The trip cost is the unit figure for the route: it prices one trip at the invoiced rate over the invoiced distance, before the frequency of the service is applied to it. The annual cost has three components, and it changes in proportion with any one of them: the distance run on each trip, the rate paid per kilometre, and the number of trips run in the year. A change in the route that lengthens the trip, a change in the invoiced rate, or a change in the service frequency each moves the annual total directly, and the total on its own does not show which component moved. The trip count includes empty running. The annual cost is therefore the cost of all running on the route, loaded and empty together, and no part of the figure is the cost of loaded running alone. The basis of the figure is the invoice record for the period: the distance, the rate, and the trip count are the invoiced quantities for that period, and the annual cost is their product, stated as a single total for the route as it was run. A comparison with another arrangement for the same route is a comparison against this total, on the same basis of distance, rate, and trips, with empty running included in the count in the same way.
